correctness.rationale: The proof covers every odd prime p>=5 and arbitrary complex unimodular f. For a two-/three-element Fourier support, a unique ordered difference forces a nonzero nonconstant Fourier coefficient of |h|^2. Three-element supports always possess such a difference by parity of inverse difference pairs; multiplicity three would give an impossible translation-invariant proper subset. Every ambiguity delay quotient is unimodular. A single-character nonzero-delay quotient solves to a chirp after p recurrence steps and c^p=1; otherwise each of p-1 nonzero delays has >=4 frequencies, plus one zero-delay coefficient. An explicit p5 construction gives exactly 17. The exact checker passes 3443 independent finite checks; these are not used to infer infinite validity.

value.rationale: Support sparsity of phase-coded prime-period radar/time-frequency ambiguity is a natural invariant. The theorem shows a structural p-to-4p-3 forbidden interval that is stronger than the sharp general p-to-2p STFT gap and independent of phase alphabet: all nonzero delays of a nonchirp must carry four or more Doppler tones. This is a meaningful exact bound for all odd prime periods, with a sharp first-prime construction. It does not claim broad noise robustness or optimality of 4p-3 for every p.
